BiblicalUsage: Lehi the place is where Samson fought with the jawbone — not the cheek itself, which shares its name. In Judges 15:19, "But God clave an hollow place that [was] in the jaw"; and in Judges 15:9, "and spread themselves in Lehi.". In Judges 15:14, "[And] when he came unto Lehi".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lehi is where God turned a jawbone into a weapon and a hollow place into a spring — Samson drank and revived there. I hold that God gives strength and water in the same place, when His servant is spent.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
